construct: SLC39A4 encodes the ZIP4 zinc uptake transporter in the small intestine. Autosomal-recessive loss of function impairs enteral zinc absorption, producing zinc deficiency with periorificial/acral dermatitis, alopecia, diarrhea, impaired wound healing, and immune dysfunction.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Post-weaning infant with chronic diarrhea, alopecia, poor growth, and periorificial/acral dermatitis has inherited zinc malabsorption from acrodermatitis enteropathica.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Hartnup disease can cause dermatitis and diarrhea, but its dermatitis is pellagra-like/photosensitive and follows neutral-amino-acid transport failure; it does not produce the classic periorificial/acral zinc-deficiency pattern linked to ZIP4.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The age and classic triad specifically support SLC39A4/ZIP4 loss of intestinal zinc uptake over the other nutrient-transport disorders.
